title: Cursor as a Planner
shortDescription: Use Cursor to break down complex tasks into actionable steps and create implementation roadmaps.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can analyze a high-level goal and decompose it into smaller, manageable tasks
It helps identify dependencies between different parts of a project
Cursor can suggest the order of implementation based on best practices
It provides a structured approach to tackling large features or refactoring work
The planning output serves as a living document that can be updated as work progresses

title: Cursor as a Pair Programmer
shortDescription: Work alongside Cursor in real-time, getting suggestions and code completions as you type.
detailedExplanation: Cursor provides intelligent code completions that understand your codebase context
It suggests implementations based on existing patterns in your project
You can ask questions about code while writing, getting immediate answers
Cursor helps maintain consistency with your project's coding style
It acts as a collaborative partner that never gets tired and has instant access to documentation

title: Cursor as a Code Reviewer
shortDescription: Have Cursor review your code for bugs, best practices, and potential improvements before committing.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can analyze code for common bugs and edge cases
It checks for adherence to best practices and design patterns
Cursor identifies potential performance issues and suggests optimizations
It reviews code for security vulnerabilities and anti-patterns
The review process helps catch issues early, before they reach production

title: Cursor as a CI Fixer
shortDescription: When CI tests fail, use Cursor to understand the errors and generate fixes automatically.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can read and interpret CI error messages and stack traces
It identifies the root cause of test failures by analyzing code and test output
Cursor suggests specific fixes for failing tests and build errors
It helps maintain code quality by ensuring all tests pass before merging
This mental model saves time by automating the debugging process for CI failures

title: Cursor as a Knowledge Retriever
shortDescription: Ask Cursor questions about your codebase to quickly understand how things work and find relevant code.
detailedExplanation: Cursor can search across your entire codebase to find relevant code and documentation
It explains how different parts of your system interact and depend on each other
Cursor helps you understand unfamiliar code by providing context and explanations
It can trace data flow and identify where specific functionality is implemented
This mental model treats Cursor as a searchable knowledge base of your project
